correctness.rationale: Classical Möbius inversion yields p^a I_{p^a}(q)=q^t(q^k-1), t=p^(a-1),k=t(p-1). For each rational prime l, q divisible by l attains valuation t at q=l; for odd l not dividing q the unit branch is zero if l-1 does not divide k (primitive residue + Dirichlet) or 1+v_l(k) if l-1 divides k (primitive root mod l² + LTE + Dirichlet). For l=2 the sharp unit valuation is 1 when k odd and v2(k)+2 when k even. Taking the minimum and subtracting a exactly at l=p gives the stated complete prime factorization. For n=2^a the odd primes l satisfy l-1 power-of-two dividing 2^(a-1), precisely prime Fermat numbers; no infinitude is asserted. Independent exact gcd over prime-power field sizes q<=80 agrees in eight (p,a) cases, including (2,5)->510. Finite checks supplement the all-prime valuation proof.
